title: New BBC ghost series inspired by 'Britain's most haunted farm' in Powys
excerpt: BBC drama The Witch Farm explores the alleged Heol Fanog haunting, Brecon Beacons folklore and Danny Robins’ Welsh story, arriving on BBC iPlayer November 22.
content:
A new BBC drama inspired by one of Wales' most notorious alleged hauntings is set to bring a chilling chapter of Brecon Beacons folklore to screens across the UK later this month.

The Witch Farm, written by Uncanny creator Danny Robins, is based on the real-life experiences of Bill and Liz Rich, who moved to the remote Heol Fanog farmhouse near Brecon in the late 1980s.

The four-part series follows a family who leave London for rural Wales in search of a fresh start, only to find themselves confronted by a series of increasingly disturbing and unexplained events.

While the television adaptation takes creative liberties, the drama is rooted in a story that has fascinated paranormal investigators and ghost story enthusiasts for decades.

Watch the trailer for The Witch Farm

Explaining how the project began, Robins said he first came across the case while searching for a follow-up to his hit BBC podcast The Battersea Poltergeist.

"I read about this couple, Liz and Bill Rich, who'd had this terrifying experience in the remote Brecon Beacons in Wales," he said.

"The more I dug into it, the more it felt like something that merited a long-form approach."

The story was first explored in Robins' BBC podcast The Witch Farm before being adapted for television.

Robins said Wales was central to both the original story and the new drama.

"This is such a Welsh story, it was so important to us to have a real Welsh accent to everything we did," he said.

"Our crew was almost entirely Welsh. It's been important that this feels like a story made and told in Wales."

The series was filmed in Wales, with production teams building a replica of the farmhouse on a soundstage while also shooting exterior scenes in the Welsh countryside.

Writer, creator and executive producer Danny Robins on the set of The Witch Farm. (Image: Simon Ridgway/Mammoth Screen/BBC)

Robins believes the landscape itself plays a major role in the story.

"The Brecon Beacons is a landscape unlike any other," he said.

"You can understand how a family could arrive there and feel like they were landing on the moon.

"It's a place where silence feels like a sound, where there is a profundity to the absence of people there, somewhere you can feel swallowed up by nature."

The drama also received support from Creative Wales and was co-commissioned by BBC Cymru Wales.

The first two episodes of The Witch Farm will be available on BBC iPlayer from November 22 and will air on BBC One and BBC One Wales the same evening.
